input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

response.prediction:
Sure! Let’s imagine a big playground where lots and lots of kids (that’s the players) want to play together at the same time. Now, imagine a grown-up (that’s the computer server) who is really good at keeping track of everyone and making sure everyone knows what the others are doing.

So, when you play an online game like CoD or WoW, your computer tells the grown-up (the server) what you’re doing—like running, jumping, or shooting. The grown-up listens to everyone playing at the same time and quickly tells everyone else what’s happening. That way, all the kids see each other moving and playing together, even if they are far away.

The grown-up is super fast and follows special rules to make sure everything runs smoothly, so it looks like everyone is playing together in the same world, all at the same time!
